messages:
sam (partnerships): Quick sync — Datadog + HW SI pre-demo checklist. We need a recommended trace sampling policy and a compact dashboard to keep ingest under control during the on-prem GPU demo. Can we agree on defaults?

anna (obs): Seeing noisy spans from the gpu model container; default 100% traces causes big spikes in DD cost. My suggestion: 1) head/always sample 10% of requests, 2) tail-sample errors/slow traces at 100%, 3) tag or mark extremely high-card spans to exclude from export.

liam (platform): Agree. For Hosted we can set a global heuristic sample_rate=0.1. For Dedicated/Private we expose per-deployment config so customers can tighten it.

ravi (eng): +1. Also prepping an OTEL Collector snippet HW SI can drop in — draft below. Keep it minimal so it works offline too.

anna (obs): please paste the snippet, that will help SI engineers.

ravi (eng): ```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
processors:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: error_policy
        type: numeric_attribute
        numeric:
          key: http.status_code
          min_value: 500
  probabilistic:
    sample_rate: 0.1
exporters:
  datadog:
    apikey: "${DD_API_KEY}"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [probabilistic, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [datadog]
```

maya (solutions): Nice. Also recommend Datadog agent settings: `apm_config.max_traces_per_second: 5` and set `apm_config.receiver_port` if customers run local agents. Add guidance for `DD_TRACE_GLOBAL_TAGS` to include `deployment:private|dedicated`.

sam (partnerships): Who will own the partner-facing doc and the marketplace listing snippet? We need something to hand to the SI before their dry-run on Wed.

anna (obs): I'll draft a short "Tracing for GPU inference" quickstart: includes the OTEL snippet, Datadog agent knobs, minimal dashboard (p50/p95 latency, trace sample rate, top noisy spans), and air-gapped notes. I'll push a PR to docs by EOD Tue.

ravi (eng): I'll add `REDWOOD_TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` env var to runtime so platform teams can flip it without redeploys. I'll include defaults and a runtime metric `redwood.trace.sample_rate` so we can audit.

liam (platform): I'll schedule a call with the Datadog PM + SI. Proposed Tue 10am PT. Sam, can you send the invite and add a short agenda?

sam (partnerships): Sending invite now. cc @eng-ops-bot to run the preflight checklist against the demo environment. :rocket:

eng-ops-bot: Preflight scheduled. Checklist items queued: invite, doc draft link, sample config, demo trace corpus. :white_check_mark:

maya (solutions): SI asked about air-gapped/offline mode for OTLP. Recommend `file` exporter + small forwarder script that retries, then a local forward pass once network restores. Add snippet to quickstart.

anna (obs): Will add a short 'Air-gapped forwarding' section with a file-exporter example and a tiny Python forwarder snippet.

sam (partnerships): Action items recap: Anna = partner doc + dashboard JSON, Ravi = runtime flag & metric, Liam = schedule & DD contact, Maya = SI notes (air-gap), Sam = invite + attach materials. Can folks ack? :eyes:

liam (platform): Ack. I'll record the call and get DD contact info.

maya (solutions): Ack. I'll prepare example demo data that shows tail-sampling benefits.

anna (obs): Ack — will upload dashboard JSON to the PR so marketing/marketplace can attach it.

ravi (eng): Ack. Default sample_rate=0.1 sounds fine for demos. No objections from infra.

sam (partnerships): Cool. One last ask — can someone export a compact Datadog dashboard JSON (no heavy widgets) we can attach to the marketplace listing by Wed morning?

anna (obs): I'll export a minimal dashboard with: trace ingestion, p50/p95 latency for inference, top 10 spans by time, and sample_rate gauge. Will attach to PR.

sam (partnerships): Perfect. Thanks everyone. Closing thread unless anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

liam (platform): Closing — will follow up with calendar invite and DD PM contact.

eng-ops-bot: Preflight checklist completed after docs PR link added.

sam (partnerships): Nice work. We'll iterate after the dry-run.
